canonical_title: Classifying evidence by method (exercised, inspected-automated, static) lets a verifier reuse CI results without duplicating deterministic work
summary: The protocol defines three evidence classes -- A (independently exercise a meaningful challenge), B (inspect authoritative automated evidence such as CI), and C (static inspection of diff/config) -- and directs the verifier not to use Class A where B or C is sufficient. It simultaneously forbids the inverse shortcut: re-running all deterministic checks locally merely to relabel Class B evidence as Class A, and requires independent execution specifically where automated coverage has a known gap (e.g. Windows-specific behavior a Linux-only CI run cannot discharge).

claims.text: The protocol defines Class A (independently exercise), Class B (inspect authoritative automated evidence such as full suites, typecheck, build, lint, Markdown gate, Full Assurance), and Class C (static inspection of dependency/workflow/provider/scope diffs), and states the verifier should not use Class A execution where Class B or C is sufficient.

evidence.locator: Section 6, 'Evidence classes': defines Class A/B/C with examples, then: 'The verifier should not use Class A execution where Class B or C is sufficient.'

claims.text: The active protocol explicitly forbids the inverse shortcut of re-running all deterministic checks locally merely to convert Class B evidence into Class A, while requiring genuine independent challenge of coverage assumptions, test weakening, and known gaps -- and explicitly states that Linux CI skipping Windows cases does not discharge Windows-specific Class A obligations.

evidence.locator: Section 6: 'Do not rerun all deterministic checks locally merely to rename Class B as Class A. Independently challenge coverage assumptions, test weakening and known gaps. Linux CI that skips Windows cases does not discharge Windows-specific Class A obligations.'

claims.text: Class B evidence is not satisfied by a green badge alone: the protocol requires confirming the correct repository/workflow/event, run attempt, tested tree, job completion, test selection and skips, and distinguishes the run head from a synthetic merge-test checkout -- explicitly stating a skipped, cancelled, queued, unavailable or still-running job is not PASS.

evidence.locator: Section 6: 'For Class B, confirm the correct repository/workflow/event, run attempt, tested tree, job completion, test selection and skips. Distinguish run head from a synthetic merge-test checkout... A job skipped, cancelled, queued, unavailable or still running is not PASS.'

conditions: Applies to any verification workflow that has access to authoritative, already-executed automated evidence (CI) and wants to avoid scarce independent-verifier time re-proving what deterministic tooling already proved.

Requires both directions of the discipline to hold simultaneously: not re-executing what CI already proved (Class A misuse), and not treating an inspected CI result as sufficient when it has a known coverage gap relative to the actual risk (Class B misuse) -- a system that only enforces one direction degrades into either wasted effort or false assurance.
anti_patterns: Independently re-running an entire deterministic suite locally as a substitute for genuinely inspecting what the authoritative CI run already proved, which wastes scarce verifier capacity without adding real information.

Accepting a green CI badge as Class B proof without checking which workflow, event, run attempt, and exact tested tree it actually covered -- a synthetic merge-test checkout, a skipped job, or a platform gap can all hide behind an apparently passing summary.
